claims.text: FCC metals such as copper are inherently ductile.
The FCC crystal structure provides multiple slip systems.
Multiple FCC slip systems permit extensive dislocation mobility during deformation.
Annealed copper has a face-centered cubic structure in its standard undeformed state.
The relevant structural mediator is the activation and mobility of dislocations along multiple slip systems associated with the FCC structure.
The availability of multiple slip systems in copper facilitates dislocation movement during deformation.
Dislocation mobility enables plastic deformation through dislocation multiplication and rearrangement.
Dislocation multiplication and rearrangement delay localized strain accumulation.
Delayed localized strain accumulation prevents brittle failure in copper.
Annealed copper will exhibit high plasticity and significant strain to failure under the stated tensile-testing conditions.
Copper will show a smooth and continuous stress-strain response during tensile deformation.
Dislocation movement on multiple slip systems will be observable during in situ microscopy.
Prior studies document the ductile behavior of annealed FCC copper under standard mechanical-testing conditions.
Extreme strain rates or very low temperatures may limit the proposed ductility mechanism.
Substantial alloying additions or impurities in copper may hinder dislocation mobility and limit the proposed behavior.
The quantitative relationship between dislocation activity and overall copper ductility across varied deformation conditions remains undetermined.
